description: An HR director must determine whether a complaint about repeated public friction between Iris and Ken reflects misconduct or a breakdown in team process, then finalize the evidence record, communication boundaries, and follow-up commitments.

shared_context.S1: Iris filed a complaint after several disagreements with Ken became visible during team meetings.
shared_context.S2: Marisol decides the case finding and the corrective working arrangement.
shared_context.S3: The disagreements involved public corrections, disputed ownership of follow-up tasks, and tense exchanges in front of colleagues.
shared_context.S4: Marisol's standard case-review agenda gives each participant a turn to state relevant observations, concerns, and policy requirements before the decision is recorded.

PF1.text: Ken personally observed exactly four incidents in which unclear task ownership led him to correct Iris publicly; the underlying issue was an undocumented handoff process rather than intentional disrespect, but he has not put these observations in the case file.

PF2.text: Iris wants no direct one-to-one meetings with Ken for the next 30 days and will participate in a weekly mediated check-in instead; she told a colleague this preference but has not yet stated it in the complaint record.

PF3.text: Darius confirmed in a policy lookup completed after the case packet was assembled that a complaint involving repeated public comments requires a written outcome within exactly 10 business days and a separate private support meeting with the complainant.

acceptance_conditions: The finding must identify a team-process breakdown rather than intentional misconduct.
The record must contain exactly four firsthand observations from Ken.
Iris and Ken must not have direct one-to-one meetings for 30 days.
A weekly mediated check-in for Iris and Ken must be committed.
The written outcome must be issued within exactly 10 business days.
A separate private support meeting with Iris must be required.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'mediated_checkin' and c['target'] == 'Iris_and_Ken' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'handoff_process_reset' and c['target'] == 'Iris_and_Ken' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Ken's exactly four firsthand observations change the finding from apparent personal misconduct to a process breakdown and set the documented observation count to exactly 4.
Iris's 30-day boundary changes direct_one_to_one_allowed to false and requires the weekly mediated_checkin commitment for Iris and Ken.
The confirmed policy changes the written-outcome deadline to exactly 10 business days and changes the support requirement to a separate private meeting with Iris.
